spans.s:
Mauṣṭika : m. (pl.): Name of a people.

As told by Karṇa to Śalya, according to the Rākṣasa Kalmāṣapāda, Mauṣṭikas were as good as the dirt of Mlecchas, and Śaṇḍas were the dirt of Mauṣṭikas (mlecchānāṁ mauṣṭikā malam/mauṣṭikānāṁ malaṁ śaṇḍāḥ) 8. 30. 70 [See P. L. Vaidya's note on the stanza, Cr. Edn.

, p. 687; “Mauṣṭikāḥ or Muṣṭikāḥ, probably a sub-caste of the Mlecchas. It is likely that the term came to be confounded with Auṣṭrikāḥ (a reading of the Central group of manuscripts), a people who made their living by trade in camels”].
